It would seem that this behavior actually broke in pydantic-core 2.29.0.

```
.venv ❯ pip list | grep pydantic         
pydantic                               2.10.6
pydantic_core                          2.28.0

~
.venv ❯ python pydantic_test.py          
pydantic version: 2.10.6
pyspark version: 4.1.1
[Package(attribute='a')]
[Package(attribute='ab'), Package(attribute='bc')]
```


After force installing 2.29.0
```
.venv ❯ pip list | grep pydantic         
pydantic                               2.10.6
pydantic_core                          2.29.0

~
.venv ❯ python pydantic_test.py          
pydantic version: 2.10.6
pyspark version: 4.1.1
[Package(attribute='a')]
26/02/10 13:36:21 ERROR Executor: Exception in task 1.0 in stage 0.0 (TID 1)/ 2]
...
AttributeError: 'Package' object has no attribute 'attribute'
```

Interesting — this happens because PySpark, when running parallel jobs, needs to serialize/deserialize using `pickle`.
I was able to reproduce the same error locally inside a Docker image. The attribute `__dict__ ` is empty when pydantic tries to apply the validator inside the worker. Note that with mode=before it works.

By the way, I would not use complex types in pyspark. Just builtins or Spark types.
```python
spark = (
    SparkSession.builder
    .appName("example")
    .master("local[*]")
    .getOrCreate()
)

class Package(BaseModel):
    attribute: str

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_model(self):
        if self.__dict__ == {}:
            raise RuntimeError("Something weird")
        assert self.attribute
        return self


def create_package(attributes):
    return [Package(attribute=attribute) for attribute in attributes]


>>> results = spark.sparkContext.parallelize(["ab", "bc"], 2).mapPartitions(create_package).collect()
RuntimeError: Something weird
```
Can you try with pydantic installed from `main`? Something similar was recently fixed (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12696).

It's worth noting, however, that I get that error without using pyspark so perhaps there's a separate bug in the main branch or in how I'm installing from the branch `pip install https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-core/archive/main.zip`.

Following a similar approach from #12696, the following two files demonstrate the problem without using pyspark.

pydantic_test_dump.py
```python
import cloudpickle
import pydantic
import pydantic_core
from pydantic import BaseModel, model_validator

class Package(BaseModel):
    attribute: str

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_model(self):
        assert self.attribute
        return self


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"  cloudpickle version: {cloudpickle.__version__}")
    print(f"     pydantic version: {pydantic.__version__}")
    print(f"pydantic_core version: {pydantic_core.__version__}")

    with open("package.pkl", "wb") as fp:
        cloudpickle.dump(Package, fp)
```

pydantic_test_load.py
```python
import cloudpickle


if __name__ == "__main__":
    with open("package.pkl", "rb") as fp:
        Package = cloudpickle.load(fp)

    print(Package(attribute="a"))
```

Sorry this is because you also need to install `pydantic-core` from `main` (which requires a Rust toolchain).

Thanks for providing the repro without pyspark. I was able to confirm it is fixed on `main`, so this is the same as https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12696. We'll be releasing a 2.13 beta really soon.
